target_customer: Brazilian households, first condominium WhatsApp groups, later online grocery shoppers wanting healthy food at lower prices
problem: Groceries pass through several middlemen so urban Brazilians pay more; Trela aimed to buy directly from suppliers and deliver to homes cheaply.
business_model: Marketplace and online grocer with take rate of about 10 percent per transaction at the start, later a just-in-time own-distribution grocery model
product_category: Social commerce and online grocery marketplace (formerly Zapt)

founders.name: Guilherme Nazareth
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2022-03) says he was a data scientist in San Francisco before moving back to Brazil; employer not named.

founders.name: Joao Jonk
founders.background_notes: Only founder named on the YC page; bio says design lover with interest in consumer brands.

founders.name: Guilherme Alvarenga
founders.background_notes: Named by TechCrunch 2022-03 and Brazilian press; background not described.

exit.reason: Company said it needed a new funding round to keep growing, did not close one and did not find the partners and terms needed to continue.

technical_complexity.rationale: A WhatsApp-driven ordering flow and web checkout were standard engineering; the hard part was physical supply chain and logistics, not software.

defensibility.rationale: Supplier relationships and delivery operations could be matched by well-funded rivals; Trela itself accused Shopper in 2025 of using exclusivity deals with suppliers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rivals with big backing entered grocery; Shopper became iFood-backed in late 2024 and Trela complained of exclusivity deals in 2025. Trela closed in April 2026.

market_need_then: Online grocery demand jumped during the pandemic and TechCrunch (2022) reported revenue up 30x since the April 2021 seed with 45 percent average monthly growth, while members saved 20 to 60 percent versus stores.

branding.domain_note: Uses trela.com.br, a Brazilian .com.br domain; a separate Brazilian fashion label also uses the name Trela.

identity.logo: Refreshed in the later years with studio Irrreal (per marketing press)
identity.voice_and_tone: Savings and fairer distribution chain messaging

rebrands.why: Not explained in sources; TechCrunch (2022-03) says formerly known as Zapt.

branding.community_and_virality: Early growth came through WhatsApp neighbor groups; Brazil Journal called it a Groupon for condominiums.

brand_strength.rationale: Known in the Brazilian startup press and by its early WhatsApp communities, but a name shared with a fashion label and no evidence of brand-led growth.

pivots.from: Zapt, group buying through WhatsApp groups in condominiums
pivots.to: Trela, social commerce marketplace for neighbors buying from suppliers
pivots.why: Not stated; name change reported by TechCrunch in March 2022.

pivots.to: Just-in-time model with own distribution center in Lapa, Sao Paulo
pivots.why: Cut costs and inventory; year approximate from press describing the pivot (PEGN title 2024-10 mentions a pivot of a pandemic thesis).

outcome_analysis: Trela rode pandemic demand for online groceries, raised a seed in April 2021 and a 25 million Series A led by SoftBank in March 2022, then pivoted away from stock-based retail toward just-in-time delivery. Online grocery was a hard-margin field where peers Justo and Mercado Diferente also closed, and Trela announced its shutdown in April 2026 after failing to close a new round.
notes: The directory lists status Active but sources report shutdown announced 2026-04-02, so exit.type shutdown conflicts with the directory and is source-backed (Startups.com.br, LatamList). trela.com.br returned HTTP 402 and could not be read. Co-founder lists conflict: YC page names Joao Jonk only; TechCrunch names Nazareth, Alvarenga and Jonk; Startups.com.br names Nazareth, Jonk and Felipe Araujo (not added). Seed was R$16M (about 3M USD per LatamList); El Referente headline says 35M in total, conflicting with 27.8M total in TechCrunch. Failure factors beyond could_not_raise_next_round are inferences from the peer-failure context and the Shopper dispute; the company's own stated cause was failure to raise. Competition at founding: TechCrunch 2022 names none and no dated 2021 rival source found, list left empty; Shopper and others appear only in 2025 to 2026 reporting.
